newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Although Finance Minister John Fahey yesterday told Prime Minister John Howard and Federal Parliament that he had sold his stake in the private firm, Tunboa Pty Ltd, in August 1986, The Australian Financial Review has learned that Fahey declared the shareolding to the New South Wales Parliament in 1995. Fahey was adamant he had disposed of his shares, even though Australian Securities Commission records showed he still owned half the company. Page 1.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission chairperson Lois O'Donoghue has attacked the Federal Government's proposed amendments to the Native Title Act, saying they contravene the principles of the 1975 Racial Discrimination Act and would reduce Abriginal people's rights to negotiate, leading to greater uncertainty. Page 2.

According to a report by US organisation Bread for the World, 14.1 per cent of Australian children under the age of 16 live below the poverty line, representing a higher proportion of children living in poverty than in any other industrialised country except the US. Page 3.

Federal Education Minister Amanda Vanstone yesterday admitted that she misled Parliament during a recent estimates committee hearing, conceding that evidence tabled during the hearing was not "spot on". Despite strong criticism of her behaviour from Victrian Labor Senator Kim Carr and Democrat higher education spokeswoman, Senator Natasha Stott Despoja, Prime Minister John Howard said he did not believe her actions would warrant her resigning. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a disappointing move for the Howard Government and business, the Reserve Bank has ruled out an early interest rate cut, warning against "excessive" wage rises. However, the bank did not reject the prospect of a future cut, provided wages were brought under control. Page 1.

Following in the footsteps of at least five other Ministers or parliamentary secretaries, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer confirmed yesterday that he was liquidating his entire share portfolio to avoid being accused of breaching the Prime Minister's code of conduct after Prime Minister John Howard "forcibly reminded" his Ministers to comply with the code. Page 1.

In the first time an Australian Parliament has been used for a free debate about euthanasia without a final vote, the New South Wales Parliament yesterday overwhelmingly rejected the concept of legalised mercy killing on a scale of four-to-one after an emtional 10-hour session. More than half the 99 members of the Lower House spoke in the debate, but in the end support for euthanasia was confined to a section of Labor left-wing MPs. Page 1.

The Microsoft Network has appointed an Australian editor to run a Sydney-based newsroom to produce stories for the first 24-hour Australian news service on the Internet. Unlike other Australian news sites, the MSN service is not based on another medium, as are The Australian and Fairfax publication sites. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the Opposition yesterday widened its attack on the Government, attacking Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer over the admission that he had disposed of more than A$60,000 worth of stock in the past few days, Prime Minister John Howard ordered his department head to examine all ministerial declarations in an attempt to clear up the shares affair. Page 1.

Following concerns from the New South Wales Labor Party Caucus that the police royal commission was protecting senior lawyers and judges involved in the pedophile inquiry, police royal commissioner Justice James Wood yesterday offered to provide State MPs with written briefings on all aspects of the commission. Page 1.

A political blunder yesterday resulted in the Government agreeing to a major policy shift on East Timor when the Senate unanimously passed a motion supporting the campaign for East Timorese independence. Previously, the Government believed that "recognising the reality" of Indonesian sovereignty was the best way to bring about positive change in East Timor. Page 1.

A courier was stabbed in the throat in Sydney's Pitt Street yesterday after he got into an argument with a man who had been blocked by the courier's van. The courier received three stitches to his throat and a 25-year-old man later presented himself to Boadway police station where he was charged with malicious wounding and common assault. Page 1.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard made it clear yesterday that he plans to tough out continuing attacks on his Ministry over conflicts of interest, despite two senior Ministers, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer and Industry Minister John Moore, coming under further pressure in Parliament. Page A1.

Controversy over hygiene in Victorian hospitals has flared again after it was revealed yesterday that according to Health Department figures, the number of full-time, State-employed cleaners in the health system had been slashed by about 40 per cent in five years. Page A1.

The Bread for the World organisation's international study has found that the poverty rate for Australian children was 14.1 per cent - worse than any other industrialised nation except for the US, on 21.5 per cent. Page A1.

Hudson Conway chief executive and Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams has ruled out opening a second casino at Tullamarine if the company succeeds in its bid to buy Melbourne Airport, stating the company was totally against gaming at the airport. Page A.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
